results.title: Trump-Linked Bitcoin Venture Reached $2.5 Million Settlement Over Improperly Obtained Loan Allegation
results.author:
Antonio Pequeño IV, Forbes Staff, 
 Antonio Pequeño IV, Forbes Staff
 https://www.forbes.com/sites/antoniopequenoiv/
results.content:
Topline
A Trump-linked cryptocurrency mining company, American Bitcoin, disclosed Monday that it settled a Justice Department allegation accusing it of improperly obtaining a pandemic relief loan, agreeing to pay millions of dollars as it omitted the settlement from its positive earnings narrative.
Key Facts
A 10-Q form filed by American Bitcoin on Monday said it agreed to pay $2.5 million to settle the allegations that Gryphon Digital Mining, a company it merged with last year, wrongfully received a Paycheck Protection Program loan, which were given out to small businesses during the height of the COVID-19 pandemic.
A filing for the quarter ended March 31 from American Bitcoin said there was “no formal demand for return of the PPP Loan proceeds, and no formal claim or lawsuit has been initiated."
The loan at the heart of the allegations was for $2.2 million and given to Gryphon when it operated as a software provider for the cannabis industry, which the Small Business Administration said made it ineligible for the PPP.
The loan was forgiven by the SBA in 2021, but the agency walked its decision back in 2024, saying in a letter it was “considering a full denial of the previously received forgiven amount” as the Justice Department issued a civil investigative demand.
Gryphon, which used to operate as Akerna, responded to the letter and argued why it believed it was eligible for the PPP loan.
Tangent
American Bitcoin shares closed up nearly 5% at $6.14 on Tuesday, continuing a series of gains after reporting earnings, which logged record bitcoin production and mentioned the settlement in the commitments and contingencies footnote.
Key Background
American Bitcoin launched last year and was co-founded by Eric Trump and Donald Trump Jr. The company was formed through a transaction in which digital compute platform Hut 8 offered its cryptocurrency mining fleet to a new entity that merged with Gryphon last September, inheriting Gryphon's legal liabilities and the PPP dispute. American Bitcoin designated the matter as an unresolved contingency through its first quarter filing this year, just disclosing it was cooperating with the Justice Department. The $2.5 million settlement exceeds the original $2.2 million loan, suggesting additional costs were added to the resolution in addition to repayment.
results.summary:
American Bitcoin, a cryptocurrency firm co-founded by Eric and Donald Trump Jr., has agreed to pay $2.5 million to settle Justice Department allegations regarding an improper pandemic loan.

### Key Points
- American Bitcoin settled claims that its subsidiary, Gryphon Digital Mining, wrongfully obtained a $2.2 million Paycheck Protection Program loan.
- The Small Business Administration deemed the loan ineligible because Gryphon operated as a cannabis industry software provider at the time of issuance.
- Although the SBA initially forgave the loan in 2021, the agency reversed that decision in 2024, prompting a federal investigation.
- The settlement amount of $2.5 million exceeds the original loan value, covering both the principal and additional resolution costs.
- American Bitcoin inherited the legal liability for the dispute following its merger with Gryphon Digital Mining last September.

### Why it Matters
This settlement resolves a significant legal contingency for a high-profile company linked to the Trump family. By finalizing the agreement, the firm mitigates ongoing regulatory uncertainty while continuing to report record cryptocurrency production to its shareholders.

results.title: Raptor PR launches Early Gaming Growth platform to help gaming startups navigate B2B communications
results.author: Sophie McEvoy
results.content:
Raptor PR has launched Early Gaming Growth (EGG), a communications platform designed for gaming startups.
The "integrated communications, reputation, and growth-building platform" aims to support early-stage companies as they build credibility to developers, publishers, and investors.
EGG also supports engagement with B2B media outlets, as well as industry creators and micro-influencers across different mediums including Substack, YouTube, newsletters, and podcasts.
It also provides support in producing content for sites such as LinkedIn, as well as blog content "that demonstrates expertise and unpacks the industry challenges affecting [a company's] audience."
"The games industry media landscape has fragmented significantly over the past five years," said Raptor PR founder and CEO Rana Rahman.
"To reach and engage a diverse range of technical stakeholders such as game developers, publishers, and investors, a multi-channel strategy is essential.
"At the same time, we're witnessing an explosion in content across all channels, with brands and people overcommunicating, making it difficult for many to reach their audiences with their messages. EGG is built on the central premise that success in B2B communications isn't about purely capturing attention, but building trust and living in the memory economy of buyers throughout complex B2B sales cycles."
PlaySafe ID CEO and co-founder Andrew Wailes added: "Early stage gaming tech is full of smart people, many of whom fall down when it comes to talking about their businesses in the right way. Founders often need guidance to better articulate their deep subject matter expertise, as it's usually obvious when a LinkedIn post has had little or no founder input.
"Long-term visibility and reputation are built over time, and it pays dividends to have the right team behind your brand. I've learned that the key is to stay consistent with communications over time, not just around major announcements or events."
results.summary:
Raptor PR has launched Early Gaming Growth (EGG), a specialized communications platform designed to help gaming startups build industry credibility and engage effectively with investors, publishers, and developers.

### Key Points
- The EGG platform provides integrated reputation management and growth-building services for early-stage gaming technology companies.
- Services include content creation for LinkedIn and corporate blogs, alongside outreach strategies for B2B media, newsletters, and podcasts.
- The platform targets engagement with industry creators and micro-influencers to navigate a fragmented media landscape.
- Raptor PR founder Rana Rahman emphasizes that the service focuses on building long-term trust rather than just capturing immediate attention.

### Why it Matters
This platform addresses the growing difficulty startups face in cutting through digital noise to reach technical stakeholders during complex B2B sales cycles. By professionalizing founder-led communications, EGG helps emerging companies establish the consistent reputation necessary to secure long-term investment and industry partnerships.
